clue.text: Zero mark given to wayward English writer

parts.note: zero looks like the letter O
a scar is a mark left on the skin
wayward means wild, out of control

explanation.surface: An unruly English author is given a score of nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Irish-born playwright is defined only as 'writer'; 'English' gives just the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: He was a celebrated Victorian playwright, novelist and wit.

clue.text: Row quiet race in America

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
the Indy, the Indianapolis 500, is a famous American motor race

explanation.surface: A dispute about a hushed American race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' is the rhymes-with-cow quarrel, not a line or rowing.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy disturbance or brawl is a row.

clue.text: Moment of truth as police force intervenes in a trial

indicators.note: the police come between parts of the other phrase, going inside it

parts.note: a test is a trial
CID, the Criminal Investigation Department, is a British police branch

explanation.surface: Detectives step into a court case at the crucial moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intervenes in' puts CID inside A TEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A decisive trial that proves whether something works is a moment of truth.

clue.text: Support for limbs of youngster learning to crawl

definitions.text: Support for limbs of youngster learning to crawl

parts.words: Support for limbs of youngster learning to crawl
parts.note: crawl is the swimming stroke, and the support is inflatable armbands for a child in the pool

explanation.walkthrough: 'Crawl' suggests a baby on all fours; it is the front-crawl swimming stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflatable armbands keep a child afloat while learning to swim.

clue.text: Nicking first of Chinamen, nearly got out

indicators.note: the letters escape their order and come out rearranged
takes only the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Stealing goods, the leading crook almost escaped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first of' gives C from Chinamen; 'got out' rearranges C + NEARLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicking is British slang for stealing, and theft is its legal name.

clue.text: A bit sedentary? Get a garden

indicators.note: only a small piece from within the word is wanted

explanation.surface: Too much sitting about? Take up gardening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit' takes the run inside sEDENtary.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical paradise was a garden.

clue.text: Actual aspect overhead of a star

indicators.note: in a down clue the aspect sits above, written before, the other word

parts.note: a side is an aspect of something
actual means real

explanation.surface: The true look of the sky above us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overhead' puts SIDE above REAL in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The astronomer's adjective means relating to the stars, as in measuring time by them.

clue.text: An assortment of people getting soft drug

parts.note: something melting is getting soft
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A mixed group of people turning soft on a drug.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where many peoples and cultures mix is a melting pot.

clue.text: Contrive to pass on something of real value

definitions.meaning: to contrive is to plan or invent

definitions.text: to pass on something of real value
definitions.meaning: in law the verb means to bequeath real property, such as land, by will

explanation.walkthrough: 'Real' is a legal pun: real property is land and buildings, not something genuinely valuable.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: invent a scheme, or leave land to an heir under a will.

clue.text: Threatening relative with seizure of home

indicators.note: a relative taking hold of something means the word for home is gripped inside it

parts.note: a sister is a family relative
in means at home

explanation.surface: A menacing family member who grabs the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with seizure of' puts IN inside SISTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something menacing or ominous seems to threaten harm.

clue.text: Quick century in search of victory

parts.note: a century in its quick, shortened form is the abbreviation C
being on a quest is being in search of something

explanation.surface: A batsman races to a hundred while chasing a win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick' signals the brief form of century, the single letter C, rather than fast scoring at the crease.
explanation.definitionFit: A triumph over an opponent, or the winning of territory, is a victory.

clue.text: Runs inside extra shed

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside another, the runs going within the extra

parts.note: a bye is a cricket extra, a run scored without the bat
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Cricket scoring talk: runs come from an extra, then someone sheds something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' places R within BYE. 'Shed' is the noun, a farm building, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowshed on a farm is the traditional rural word for this building.

clue.text: This Bertie was a swell Palladian architect

definitions.meaning: a music-hall song of 1915 celebrated a Bertie who was a dandy about town
the 3rd Earl of this title was a leading champion of Palladian architecture in Georgian England

explanation.walkthrough: The music-hall song character 'Burlington Bertie' was a penniless would-be toff.
explanation.definitionFit: The music-hall dandy and the Georgian earl who built in the Palladian style share the name.

clue.text: Put on air originally, it offers view of the way ahead

definitions.text: it offers view of the way ahead

indicators.note: says the air comes at the start, at the origin of the answer, before the other piece

parts.note: wind is moving air
to screen a programme is to put it on, to broadcast or show it

explanation.surface: A broadcasting note about putting something on air first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' puts WIND at the front, before SCREEN. 'Put on air' looks like a broadcasting phrase but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's front glass panel lets the driver see the road in front.

clue.text: What might one bid for armour?

definitions.meaning: in bridge a player bids in the long, high-scoring holding of one kind of card
protective metal clothing is a tough set of garments

explanation.walkthrough: 'bid' suggests an auction; it is a bridge call, and 'suit' doubles as clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridge player bids in a long, high-scoring holding, and a set of armour is tough clothing.

clue.text: Lying about not working

definitions.meaning: lying about is lounging, taking a break
an actor between jobs is said to be in this state

explanation.walkthrough: The theatre euphemism for an actor out of work is the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a break while lounging, and being out of work, as actors euphemistically say, are both meant.

clue.text: Start to suck up to media censor

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the press is the news media

explanation.surface: Begin flattering the newspapers to keep a story quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start' takes S from suck. 'suck up to' reads as flatter, but it splits apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To censor a report is to stop it being published.

clue.text: Baggage lines protected by armed force

indicators.note: the lines are shielded within the armed force, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: a troop is a body of soldiers

explanation.surface: Luggage with its lines guarded by soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protected by' puts LL inside TROOP. 'Baggage' is the old insult for a disreputable woman, not luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are old-fashioned insulting words for a promiscuous or disreputable woman.

clue.text: Native of Mediterranean area, not a settler

definitions.meaning: someone from the Levant, the eastern Mediterranean coast
to levant is old slang for running off without paying debts, so such a person does not settle up

explanation.walkthrough: 'settler' suggests a colonist; it means one who settles a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: The name means someone from the eastern Mediterranean, and also one who absconds without paying debts.

clue.text: Powerful unfinished set of poems that may transport us

indicators.note: the word for powerful loses its last letter, left without an ending

parts.note: big means powerful
a cycle is a set of linked poems or songs

explanation.surface: A mighty poetry sequence, left incomplete, could carry us away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts G from BIG. 'transport us' sounds like poetic rapture but means carrying riders.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-wheeled pedalled machine carries riders from place to place.

clue.text: Remarkable effect of mimicry

definitions.meaning: an effect worth remarking on, as in making a mark on someone
an impersonation of a famous person by a comic

explanation.definitionFit: Leaving a strong mark on people, and a comedian's imitation of someone, are both meant.

clue.text: Force unit to rebel, after soldiers leave the front

indicators.note: the soldiers depart from the start of the word for rebelling, taking its opening letters away

parts.note: to revolt is to rebel
RE, the Royal Engineers, is a common crossword abbreviation for soldiers

explanation.surface: An army unit rises up after the troops abandon the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leave the front' removes RE from the start of REVOLT. Military words fill the surface, but 'Force unit' is physics.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the SI unit of electromotive force, or electrical potential difference.

clue.text: Officer consumed by desire is a pest

indicators.note: the officer is eaten up, swallowed inside the word for desire

parts.note: lust is strong desire
OC is short for Officer Commanding

explanation.surface: A commander eaten up by longing is a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumed by' puts CO inside LUST.
explanation.definitionFit: A swarming grasshopper that strips crops is a classic plague insect.

clue.text: Boy accepts a little taste — it's pungent

indicators.note: the boy takes in the taste, holding it inside his name

parts.note: Gary is a boy's name
a lick is a small taste, as of ice cream

explanation.surface: A lad tries a small sample of something strong-flavoured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepts' puts LICK inside GARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Food strongly flavoured with this bulb has a sharp, pungent smell.

clue.text: Abandon beginning of speech

indicators.note: tells us the word for a beginning is heard spoken, not written

parts.note: a seed is the beginning from which something grows

explanation.surface: Giving up at the start of an address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of speech' signals a word that is said rather than written: SEED.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up territory or rights is to surrender them, abandoning the claim.

clue.text: Pronounce Boxer Rising, say, to have been too late

definitions.text: Pronounce Boxer Rising, say, to have been too late

parts.words: Pronounce Boxer Rising, say, to have been too late
parts.note: a referee declares a floored fighter beaten when he gets up only after ten seconds have been called

explanation.surface: A historian rules that China's Boxer uprising of 1900 came too late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer Rising' suggests the Chinese rebellion; read it as a fighter rising from the canvas too late to beat the referee's ten.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee declares a downed fighter defeated after ten seconds on the canvas.

clue.text: Used to suffering and being put out

indicators.note: suffering means hurt or damaged, so the letters are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: Someone accustomed to hardship and to being thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' rearranges USEDTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Being expelled or removed from a position is being put out.

clue.text: Make very happy about 'Arry's college

indicators.note: the word for delight goes around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: to elate is to make very happy
Cockney 'Arry drops his H; to harry is to hector, so the dropped-H version of hector is ECTOR

explanation.surface: Cockney Harry's college makes someone delighted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ECTOR inside ELATE. 'Arry is Harry with the dropped H of Cockney speech, so harry = hector loses its H too.
explanation.definitionFit: An electoral college is a body of voters, so the word for all voters fits 'college'.
